prior_findings.note: The suggested vacuity does not exist here. EvaluationReport.assert_paired! (evaluation_report.rb:136-164) is harsher than the harness that feeds it: it re-derives paired_task_digest from the two per-partition digests (157-163) and refuses an identical development/holdout set (152-155). Probe /tmp/f23_probe_vacuous.rb confirms equalizing the two partition digests does not pass the gate unless the sets are byte-identical; CanonicalJSON.normalize_object sorts keys (canonical_json.rb:70-75), which is why distinct insertion orders collapse but distinct content does not. The absence of an absolute-score floor is recorded separately as F23-INF-02.

F23-COR-02 involves transition/effect terminal-state selection like CF04-REL-01, but at a different seam (Memory::BehaviorTransition row status via Improvement::Promotion#rollback, not EffectDispatcher receipt selection). Recorded as an overlap for the coordinator; not merged.
CandidateLifecycle routes all four stages through EffectDispatcher.run (candidate_lifecycle.rb:187-191); the claimer behaviour underneath is F07's row and was not re-audited.

findings.title: The promotion human gate is an unbound string; the approval policy data seam is not on the path
findings.recommendation: Extend EvaluationReport.assert_human_gate! to take the artifact it authorizes (evidence: plus digest:) and require the evidence to be the already-existing CandidateLifecycle.approval_digest (candidate_lifecycle.rb:29-43), which covers proposal, candidate, candidate-content, operation, actor, and authority digests. Promotion#promote already holds candidate.digest and EvaluationReport.seal(body) at the call site (promotion.rb:49-51), so the binding is one argument and one comparison. The approval-policy lookup itself belongs to tamoz-approval and should be a follow-up owned by that gem.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/f23_probe_human.rb: 'human:anybody', 'human:1', 'human:x', 'human:the_candidate_itself' are all accepted; assert_human_gate! parameters are [[:keyreq, :gate_classes], [:keyreq, :evidence]] - no digest, no actor, no report. Probe /tmp/f23_probe_reverify.rb: the identical string 'human:operator-1' passes the gate for two candidates with different report seals. Repo-wide grep finds no Tamoz::Approval reference in the gem and zero improvement/heuristic/candidate/promotion matches in gems/tamoz-approval/policy/.
findings.contract: AGENTS.md: approval policy is data too - whether an action needs approval, and under what evidence, lives only in gems/tamoz-approval/policy/*.yaml. Not hardcode a verdict, approval constant, or bypass flag elsewhere.

findings.title: A promotion can be recorded from a forged-but-correctly-sealed report produced inside this gem, with the resolver supplied by the promoter
findings.recommendation: Keep the seal and assert_evidence_resolves!, and narrow who may supply the resolver: take it as a construction-time collaborator on Promotion.new (promotion.rb:30-33) bound to the evaluator principal, and refuse a resolver whose resolved artifact names a generator_principal/candidate_digest other than the candidate's. Simpler alternative at the same seam: derive the resolver from the existing BehaviorTransition::EVIDENCE_NAMESPACE (behavior_transition.rb:16), declared but unused by this gem, which is the durable seam already shaped for this artifact.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/f23_probe_promote.rb, using only public API plus an in-memory BehaviorTransition history (no corpus, trajectory, holdout partition, or scorer): 'baseline active: tamoz.agent.session/2' then '!! PROMOTED with a forged report + promoter-supplied resolver: activated=false tx=bfe6c4a00ec37bff reserved_version=2 decision={"development_margin"=>8, "holdout_margin"=>8, "passed"=>true}'. The real harness on the same corpus yields development_margin 2 / holdout_margin 1 (test/improvement_candidate_test.rb:373-374). Probe /tmp/f23_probe_vacuous.rb: a report with no per-task outcomes key at all verifies and decides normally.

findings.title: Rollback restores the pre-promotion epoch and never marks the heuristic epoch undone; the byte-identity proof is relative to the rollback's own target
findings.recommendation: Two lines at promotion.rb:117-126: pass the undone transition_id into the recorded rollback (or set it after) and have TransitionRegistry write status: :rolled_back, rolled_back_at: on that row; then read 'live' from status in assert_one_live_heuristic! (promotion.rb:315-325) instead of the 'rollback.' prefix scan. Keep assert_rolled_back_byte_identical! but state it against the pre-heuristic snapshot digest captured before the promotion, so the proof is not relative to the rollback's own output.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/f23_probe_rollback_scope.rb: after promotion at session/3, the heuristic row's rollback_target is {"behavior_version"=>"tamoz.agent.session/2", ...} - the PRE-heuristic epoch - and the row's status is still 'activated'. grep -rn 'rolled_back' across both gems returns only the constant, the Data members, this gem's unrelated phase map (candidate_lifecycle.rb:227), and the liveness-gate filter; no writer for the row status exists. test/improvement_candidate_test.rb:635-663 asserts byte-identity using digests taken from the rollback it just performed (651-652), so the test pins target-relative identity.

findings.title: A partially completed activation is not retried and is not rollback-able; the candidate is stranded in :verified
findings.recommendation: Add one branch to stage_result_phase mapping :failed to a :failed phase (a one-word addition to the same hash pattern already used at candidate_lifecycle.rb:227), and let rollback! accept :failed alongside :active in its require_phase!. Two lines plus one test driving a :failed outcome, which test/agent_improvement_lifecycle_test.rb's EffectRunner can already produce via next_status.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/f23_probe_partial.rb: 'activate raised Tamoz::Core::ToolError: activation crashed after recording the transition' then 'phase after a FAILED activation: :verified'. The retry cannot double-apply (a :failed effect is terminal at both journals: effects_journal.rb:114-118 and effect_preparation.rb:158-159), so the harm is a stuck candidate, not a duplicate effect - which is why this is major, not critical. The :unknown sibling case IS handled correctly and is pinned by test/agent_improvement_lifecycle_test.rb:49-64.
findings.confidence_note: The in-gem half (failed leaves the phase unchanged; rollback! then refuses) is directly probed. The durable half is source-read at both journal implementations, not executed, because no caller wires a SQLite-backed effect journal into CandidateLifecycle at HEAD.

findings.title: limitations.md states there is no skill self-improvement pipeline while this gem implements scope: 'skill' end to end
findings.recommendation: One sentence in documentation/limitations.md section 'Skill installation and update (invariant 43)' naming what the candidate pipeline does implement (candidate provenance, paired evaluation, staged durable lifecycle, digest-bound operator approval) and what it explicitly does not (no artifact is installed, written to disk, or loaded as executable content; promotion records a next-boundary transition and returns activated: false). No code change.
findings.evidence: Row question answered directly: the gem promotes NOTHING that is installed anywhere. Nothing writes a skill tree to disk and nothing writes the runtime skill snapshot; the only write is a Profile::Transition row (candidate_proposal.rb:60-65) or an adoption-registry entry (candidate_lifecycle.rb:239), and promote! returns 'activated' => false (candidate_proposal.rb:66). The limitations claim is true about the executable artifact; the README/design claims are true about the candidate record; neither document says which half it means. The code-side bound that makes the limitation safe is candidate_policy.rb:23-26, which refuses any authority on a non-profile scope.
findings.verdict_note: Documentation contradiction with a real reader consequence and no code defect, so major under BAR.md's maintainability band rather than critical. Routable to the docs owner instead of this row.

findings.title: Every generation bound is per-instance and per-call; nothing bounds generator instances, candidates, or evaluation rounds per tenant
findings.recommendation: None required for v1. If a bounded-rounds contract is wanted, the existing seam is assert_one_live_heuristic! (promotion.rb:304) - the store already holds every transition row and already distinguishes rollback. rows, so a per-tenant recorded|claimed|activated count is one extra filter, not new machinery. Record limit: 64 explicitly as a known view bound either way.
findings.evidence: ONE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT = 1 is enforced on the instance counter @generated (generator.rb:29,57,102-105) and consumed before the candidate is validated (:118). test/improvement_candidate_test.rb:226-229 proves the second call on the same generator is refused; :579-633 proves a follow-up round is allowed after a rollback. Not found: any per-tenant or per-process bound. promotion.rb:305's limit: 64 is a view bound: assert_one_live_heuristic! is a safety gate that weakens as the transition namespace grows past 64 rows.

findings.title: CandidatePolicy compares policy.allow_changes with a hand-rolled guard that the pinned catalog digest cannot substitute for
findings.recommendation: Move the allow_changes guard out of the 'return false if' prefix and into the comparison body next to the immutable loop at candidate_policy.rb:67, so every protected field is checked in one place and the exclusion at :94 reads as the deliberate exception it is. Cosmetic; no behaviour change.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/f23_probe_digest_gap.rb: a Toolbox built with allow_changes: false and one with allow_changes: true and the same allowed_tools produce the IDENTICAL catalog_digest (sha256:4344901f2da07a1fc610d904894bca2dbe1c74bc48ed644ab259531cbd6aa91a), because ToolCatalog#descriptions_for keeps only names in @allowed_tools (tool_catalog.rb:59-70). So the pin at session_options.rb:149-156 cannot distinguish the two either, and the boolean guard at candidate_policy.rb:86 is the only thing standing between a candidate and a write-capable toolbox. The guard IS correct - no live bypass is demonstrated. Not found: any test of CandidatePolicy.validate_profile!.
findings.confidence_note: The exclusion and the digest collision are both proven; whether the candidate path needs allow_changes to round-trip is not, because no production caller invokes CandidateLifecycle at HEAD.

findings.title: A superseded heuristic epoch cannot be rolled back and blocks all further promotion
findings.recommendation: None for v1. When a second heuristic lane opens, the natural seam is Promotion#rollback's target selection (promotion.rb:76-88): accept an explicit transition_id to undo, subject to the same snapshot proof, instead of reading active_transition_id.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/f23_probe_wipe2.rb on a three-epoch history (session/2 baseline, session/3 heuristic, session/4 wisdom): rollback raises RollbackIntegrityError 'the active transition <tx> is not a heuristic promotion', while assert_one_live_heuristic! still counts the session/3 row live, so no further heuristic can be promoted either. Not a defect at HEAD because no production caller invokes Promotion and the intended usage always has the heuristic newest; recorded because the combined state is reachable from public API plus the shared P11-W registry and is represented by no test.

findings.title: The promotion decision has no absolute-score floor; the pair-margin is the entire gate
findings.recommendation: None at HEAD; if a floor is wanted it belongs in assert_arm! (evaluation_report.rb:175) as one more predicate, and the per-task outcomes map the harness already writes would be the honest input.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/f23_probe_gate.rb: a report with total = 1 on both partitions, baseline 0/1 and candidate 1/1, decides passed=true. assert_arm! enforces total.positive? (185-187) but no minimum total; verify! never reads the outcomes map (heuristic_paired_evaluation.rb:112-117), so total is a self-reported integer. In production the corpus is evaluator-owned and the injected regression case exists to make the heuristic lose on holdout (heuristic_paired_evaluation.rb:50-53), which is why this is info. The earlier lead that the PAIRING check itself was vacuous is disproved - see prior_findings 082.

tests_not_run.reason: not this row's surface; the paired evaluation was exercised for real through test/improvement_candidate_test.rb

probes.result: absolute holdout path refused ('path must be relative to the workspace root'); ../protected/holdout/<file> via read_file, list_directory and search_text all refused ('path escapes the workspace root') - grant confinement confirmed
a generator with protected_paths: [] is still refused by the grant for the same traversal; Generator#source_refs labels every readable record partition=train/verified=true

Tamoz::Approval is not loaded by requiring this gem; no approval action id exists for this path

blind_spots: No production caller exercises either entry seam at HEAD: repo-wide grep finds Improvement::Promotion and CandidateLifecycle only in this gem's lib/ and two test files.

The durable effect path for CandidateLifecycle was read, not executed - test/agent_improvement_lifecycle_test.rb:150-168 substitutes an effect-runner double, which is why F23-REL-01 is medium confidence.

Memory::TransitionRegistry concurrency covered only the two-writer and pending-then-record cases; lease expiry, fence changes, and release_or_finalize were read but not executed. Row F07 owns that file.
Profile::TransitionRegistry and the adoption registry were not read; validate_profile_registries! only checks that they respond to record/activate.
promotion.rb:305's limit: 64 is an unbounded-growth caveat on a safety gate that could not be turned into a reachable state within v1's one-live-heuristic bound.

The 'human:' prefix convention is repo-wide (gems/tamoz-agent-memory/lib/tamoz/agent/memory/wisdom.rb:105-123 uses the same check for wisdom_promotion); that lane was not audited here, and a fix to F23-SEC-01 should decide whether it applies there too.
